_why: Which sections of the canonical replay document BOTH sides can produce today.
The differential layer lands module by module: curve_ref.py mirrors auction.rs, settle_ref.py
mirrors settle.rs and finalize_round, claims_ref.py mirrors claims.rs. The Python side has all
three; the Rust side has whichever replays exist. So the diffable scope is smaller than the
Python document for as long as that is true, which 06-TEST-PLAN §5 and D-22's deadline rule
both require rather than merely tolerate.
This file is the single home for that scope, and it is self-checking in both directions:
run_vectors.py --out emits exactly these sections, and test_vectors.rs asserts that what it
emits is exactly these sections. Adding a Rust replay without widening this list fails the
Rust test; widening the list without adding the replay fails the diff. Neither side can drift
from it silently, which is the property a hand-maintained scope would not have.
To widen: add the section here in the same commit as the Rust replay that produces it.

not_yet_replayed_in_rust.settle_ref: needs finalize_round driven from a Rust replay - DEV1/DEV2
not_yet_replayed_in_rust.claims_ref: needs claims.rs, which DEV3 has not written yet
